schema: Published body-proportion measurements (fraction of standard length, SL) of Monte Bolca (Ypresian, ~50 Ma) fossil fishes belonging to families sampled in the Claverie & Wainwright (2014) landmark set. Used by thompson/run_phylogenetic_prediction_engine.py to test the predicted state of each family's lineage at the fossil's age. Ratio keys: BDmax_over_SL = maximum body depth excluding fin webs / SL; HL_over_SL = head length (snout to posterior border of opercle) / SL; PD_over_SL = predorsal length (snout to first dorsal-fin spine) / SL. Values are single numbers or [low, high] ranges exactly as reported (or as derived from reported 'contained N times in SL' statements).
age_note: Pesciara site, late Ypresian, Alveolina dainellii Zone (SBZ 11), c. 49-50 Ma (Papazzoni & Trevisani 2006; Papazzoni et al. 2014). Older literature dates the same beds as 'lower Middle Eocene / Lutetian'.

Bellwoodilabrus_landinii.placement: Labridae; unique combination of plesiomorphic and derived features (position within the family unresolved)
Bellwoodilabrus_landinii.source: Bannikov A.F. & Carnevale G. (2010) Geodiversitas 32(2): 201-220, 'Measurements (as percentage of SL)': HL 31, maximum body depth 41, snout to first dorsal-fin spine 42. Holotype MCSNV IGVR 71214/71215, 34 mm SL.

Palaeopomacentrus_orphae.placement: oldest substantiated pomacentrid; 'relatively generalized Recent pomacentrid' body form
Palaeopomacentrus_orphae.source: Bellwood D.R. & Sorbini L. (1996) Zool. J. Linn. Soc. 117: 159-174. Holotype MCSNV IG 23692: SL 20.5 mm, maximum body depth 9.0 mm (43.9%); paratype BMNH P.5126: SL 29.5 mm, depth 15.0 mm (50.8%).

Sparnodus_elongatus.placement: Sparidae (Sparnodus); value is the deepest-bodied Sparnodus specimen recorded (holotype of 'Pomadasys' furcatus = S. elongatus), typical individuals are shallower
Sparnodus_elongatus.source: Bannikov A.F. (2006) Geodiversitas 28(2): 249-275: 'SL/maximum body depth ratio is 2.1' for MNHN Bol 68/69, 'equal in depth to the most deep-bodied specimens of Sparnodus ever recorded'.
Sparnodus_elongatus.note: upper bound for the genus; no typical-specimen value is given in the source

Goujetia_crassispina.placement: Sparidae (new genus for Dentex crassispinus Agassiz)
Goujetia_crassispina.source: Bannikov A.F. (2006) Geodiversitas 28(2): 249-275: head length contained 3.25 times in SL (30.8%); head length 1.17 times less than body depth (-> 36.0% SL). Holotype MNHN Bol 8/9, 128 mm SL.

Ottaviania_leptacanthus.source: Bannikov A.F. (2006) Geodiversitas 28(2): 249-275, diagnosis: 'Head length 3.03 in SL. Maximum body depth 3.26 in SL.' Holotype MNHN Bol 14a/14b, 261 mm SL.

Veranichthys_ventralis.placement: Lutjanidae (new genus for Serranus ventralis Agassiz)
Veranichthys_ventralis.source: Bannikov A.F. (2006) Geodiversitas 28(2): 249-275, Table 3 (lectotype MNHN Bol 275 and paralectotype Bol 24): head length 32 (30), maximum body depth 34 (34), snout to spiny dorsal fin 40 (39) % SL.

Ruffoichthys_bannikovi.placement: stem Siganidae (most basal fossil siganid genus in Tyler & Bannikov 1997)
Ruffoichthys_bannikovi.source: Tyler J.C. & Bannikov A.F. (1997) Smithsonian Contributions to Paleobiology 84: 'the greatest body depth is 41%-43% SL in R. bannikovi versus 23%-34% in R. spinosus'.

Ruffoichthys_spinosus.source: Tyler J.C. & Bannikov A.F. (1997) Smithsonian Contributions to Paleobiology 84 (see R. bannikovi).

Eoleiognathus_dorsalis.placement: putative stem Leiognathidae (new subfamily Eoleiognathinae); formerly 'Pygaeus dorsalis'
Eoleiognathus_dorsalis.source: Bannikov A.F. (2014) Studi e Ricerche sui Giacimenti Terziari di Bolca XV: neotype MCSNV T94/T95, 24.5 mm SL, maximum body depth 48% SL.

Eoplatax_papilio.placement: Ephippidae, closely allied to Platax (Blot 1969; Carnevale et al. 2014)
Eoplatax_papilio.source: No published ratio located (Blot 1969 monograph not online). Range estimated by the author from two photographed specimens: MCSNV specimen (Wikimedia Commons 'Eoplatax papilio 376.jpg', CC BY-SA 4.0, Ghedoghedo) and NHMW specimen (Wikimedia Commons 'Eoplatax Vienna.jpg', CC BY 2.0), measuring body depth at the dorsal/anal fin bases (excluding the elongate fin webs) over snout-to-hypural length. Blot (1969) describes the body as about as deep as, or deeper than, long.
Eoplatax_papilio.note: photograph-derived estimate; the discriminating question (deep Platax-like body vs. the 0.57-0.77 stem prediction) is robust to the measurement uncertainty
